M2 package - NVIDIA G86 hardware detection (scans out via VESA, adds native probe)

What this is: the same working VESA framebuffer desktop as M1, PLUS our own
code that finds the G86 on the PCI bus, maps its MMIO, and reads the chip ID
(PMC_BOOT_0). It does NOT yet drive the GPU natively. Goal of this step: prove
our code can see and talk to the real chip.

Files:
  nvmini.vxd      - 32-bit VxD: VESA scanout + NV_probe (chip detection)
  nvmini.drv      - 16-bit DIBENG display driver (companion)
  vmdisp9x.inf    - installs the pair; bound to PCI\VEN_10DE&DEV_0429 (NVS 140M)
  nvprobe.exe     - Win32 tool that reads the probe result (no serial needed)

Install on the T61 (Win98 SE), fully reversible:
  1. In Safe Mode, set the display adapter to "Standard Display Adapter (VGA)"
     (removes the broken stock NVIDIA driver). Reboot to a VGA desktop.
  2. Copy all four files to e.g. C:\NVMINI\ .
  3. Control Panel > Display > Settings > Advanced > Adapter > Change >
     Have Disk > C:\NVMINI\vmdisp9x.inf. Pick
     "NVIDIA Quadro NVS 140M (G86) [native, T61]". Finish, reboot.
  4. Expected: a working desktop (via VESA), same as M1.
  5. Open an MS-DOS Prompt (or Run) and run C:\NVMINI\nvprobe.exe.
     Report the full output. Success looks like:
        chipset : 0x86  family 0x08  ...  mmio_ok 1
        => G86 confirmed. We can talk to the chip.

If the desktop does not come up: fall back to Standard VGA in Safe Mode and
report what happened. If the desktop works but nvprobe reports mmio_ok 0 or a
wrong chipset, that is still useful - send the BOOT0/BAR values it prints.


UPDATE 2026-10-21 (build 3033 package):
  - Also copy SYSTEM.INI over C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM.INI and merge nvsetup.reg
    (regedit /s nvsetup.reg). Never add IgnoreRegistry=1 to [Display]: the
    Win98 VDD reads that key and then does not load nvmini.vxd at all.
  - To check what really loaded, use a logged boot's BOOTLOG.TXT, not DxDiag.
  - Build 3035: after any boot run  nvprobe log > nvlog.txt  - it holds the
    debug output of both nvmini.vxd (V>) and nvmini.drv (D>) for that boot.
    nvmini.drv also appends its lines to C:\NVMINI.LOG - send that file too.
  - Full findings and the current diagnostic checklist:
    analysis/BOOT_DIAGNOSIS_2026-10-21.md in the repo.

UPDATE 2026-10-22 (build 3037): the reason nvmini.drv NEVER loaded (LoadFail
0000) was a bad NE relocation produced by the toolchain from a __segname("_TEXT")
declaration in init.c; fixed. Install the three 3037 files, keep SYSTEM.INI
display.drv=nvmini.drv and the nvsetup.reg values, reboot. Expect
'LoadSuccess = nvmini.drv' in a logged BOOTLOG.TXT and a 1024x768 desktop.

=====================================================================
INSTALL FROM THE INF ALONE (build 3039+, M4.2)
=====================================================================
1. Copy the whole package folder to the T61 (e.g. C:\NVMINI).
2. Device Manager > the display adapter (on the T61 it is the root
   "Standard Display Adapter (VGA)" node, *PNP0900; the PCI NVIDIA node also
   matches) > Properties > Driver > Update Driver > Have Disk > C:\NVMINI >
   pick "NVIDIA Quadro NVS 140M (G86) [native, T61 root VGA node]" (or the
   [native, T61] entry on the PCI node). Finish, reboot.
   The INF writes drv/minivdd, Mode=16,1024,768, DDC=0 (no 3-minute EDID
   probe) and Native=1. SYSTEM.INI stays at display.drv=pnpdrvr.drv.
3. After the reboot pick resolution/colour in Display Properties.
4. Only if something is off: nvsetup.reg re-applies the registry values,
   SYSTEM.INI (this folder) is a known-good reference, and
   "nvprobe log > nvlog.txt" shows what the driver did.


DIRECTDRAW (build 3044+)
------------------------
DirectDraw needs the ring-3 HAL from JHRobotics/vmhal9x, shipped here as
vmhal9x.dll, vmdisp9x.dll and vmhal3d.dll (built against this driver's FBHDA
API version; do NOT mix with the DLLs from an upstream vmdisp9x release).
  - Fresh INF install: copied to C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM automatically.
  - Existing install: copy the three DLLs to C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM. No reboot
    needed - DirectDraw loads the HAL when an application starts.
Check: DXDIAG -> Display tab -> "DirectDraw Acceleration: Enabled", then
"Test DirectDraw". Diagnostics: C:\NVMINI.LOG or 'nvprobe log' shows
"DDGET32BITDRIVERNAME: success" and "DDCREATEDRIVEROBJECT: success".

DIRECT3D (build 3045+)
----------------------
Direct3D (DDI 8: DirectX 6/7/8-era, and DX9 titles without shaders) renders
in software through Mesa9x. Needed in C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM: vmhal3d.dll (from
3044) and mesa3d.dll (44 MB, from 3045). The INF copies both; on an existing
install copy mesa3d.dll there and import d3dsetup.reg. Check: DXDIAG ->
Display -> "Direct3D Acceleration: Enabled", then "Test Direct3D".

GPU OPENGL - HALF-LIFE (build 3093+)
------------------------------------
Hardware-accelerated OpenGL (Mesa's nv50 driver on the G86) is opt-in per
program through the environment: set GALLIUM_DRIVER=nouveau in the DOS box
that starts the program. Without it the ICD renders in software as before.
Half-Life: copy nvhl.bat and mesa3d.dll from this package into the Half-Life
folder (next to hl.exe), edit NVDRV in nvhl.bat to this package's folder, then
in a DOS box in the Half-Life folder run:  nvhl  (or nvhl -width 640 -height 480).
The batch sets GALLIUM_DRIVER=nouveau and MESA_EXTENSION_MAX_YEAR=2000 (the
GoldSrc extension-string overflow), starts the VxD log tail, runs hl.exe and
leaves C:\nvshim.log, C:\nvtail.txt, C:\nvkick.txt for diagnosis. In the
game, Video options -> OpenGL, "Default" driver, 640x480 or 800x600.
wgltest's "texture" scene (wgltest driver mesa3d.dll window texture) is the
driver-side rehearsal of what a game needs (mipmapped textures, dynamic
texture updates, depth, fog, blending, alpha test).
wgltest's "stress" scene (build 3095+: wgltest driver mesa3d.dll window stress) is a
GoldSrc-shaped frame (600 glBegin/glEnd quads over 72 textures, 32 lightmap patches,
50 indexed draws) - its 'present frames/ms' is the driver's draw-call ceiling.
The autoexec.cfg in the half-life folder is the SOFTWARE-renderer speed config; on
the GPU path it is optional (r_dynamic 0 and gl_picmip 1 still cut texture updates
and texture memory).
Build 3106 - present A/B switches (mesa3d.dll only; copy it next to hl.exe too - the
3105 log showed Half-Life still loading the 3099 mesa3d.dll: nvshim.log must start with
"vxd build / shim build 00000c22 00000c22"). On the T61, 3105's corner blocks stayed with
gl_clear 1 but vanished with the CPU present, so the rendered frame is right and the GPU
present - the 2D-engine blit of the window buffer into the screen surface - shows them.
Three runs at 1024x768, grctx0, same map and spot:
  nvhl barrier    a cache barrier between the frame's drawing and the blit
  nvhl present3d  the 3D engine copies the frame (textured quad) instead of the 2D blit
  nvhl vsync      the blit waits for the vertical blank (if not tried yet)
Report for each: blocks yes/no, and the fps line. Photos of the blocks still wanted.

Build 3105 - mesa3d.dll upload fix (the VxD is 3104 with a new stamp; copy BOTH
nvmini.vxd and mesa3d.dll - the one next to hl.exe too - then reboot once). A buffer
mapped write-only assumed its VRAM already held zeros, so any 1 KiB chunk the program
filled entirely with zeros (black texture rows, lightmap patches, unused constant slots)
was never uploaded and the GPU read the previous buffer's bytes there. Found by an
independent review; reproducer tools/repro_nvshim_zero_upload.py. Not yet proven to be
the corner squares. Tests for the squares, all grctx0 and all in ONE Half-Life run at
1024x768: (1) does 3105 still show them; (2) console "gl_clear 1" - do the squares
become the clear colour (= uncovered pixels) or stay garbage; (3) from a DOS box
"set NVSHIM_CPU_PRESENT=1" then nvhl (slow; CPU copies the frame instead of the GPU
blit) - squares gone = the present path, still there = rendering. A photo of the
squares helps more than any log.

Build 3104 - 3103 fixed. Its "handle bound again" test looked in the channel's hash table,
which the channel init pre-seeds with the VxD's own 2D handle 0xbeef502d, so the very first
GL program's own 0xbeef502d bind already counted as a "second process": the channel was
rebuilt in the middle of the screen setup and the new 2D/3D objects overwrote the memory
objects bound just before - the first 3D submit hung the GPU (gray nvsky window; Half-Life
crashed inside mesa3d.dll once the shim heap filled with buffers that never retired).
3104 only counts the handles the GL programs bound themselves. Same retest as 3103:
several programs per boot, grctx0 (nvsky, nvsky 800 600, nvhl), then grctx4, then grctx3.
C:\nvtail.txt must show "bound again -> new GL process" only at the START of the 2nd, 3rd...
program (right after its first bind, BEEF0201), never in the middle of one.

Build 3103 - one GPU channel per GL program. The 3102 logs explained "nvsky 1024x768 fine,
nvsky 800x600 garbage, Half-Life garbage": the GPU channel is built by the FIRST GL program
after a boot and, until now, every later program reused it (same objects bound twice, the
dead program's engine state inherited) - only the first GL program after a boot ever drew
correctly (3099's Half-Life, 3100's and 3102's first nvsky), every later one was garbage at
9 fps, whatever the context variant. The GrCtx value was also only read at that first
creation, so the grctx1..4 switches never took effect. Now the second GL program rebuilds
the channel from cold (C:\nvtail.txt: 'bound again -> new GL process, rebuilding the
channel' followed by 'grctx variant N'), so the registry switch really works per GL start.
Please retest in this order, several programs per boot: grctx0 (the 3099 context): nvsky,
nvsky 800 600, nvhl at 1024x768 (expected: all clean except the corner holes); then grctx4
(holes gone?); then grctx3.

Build 3102 - the 1024x768-only corner holes checked against NVIDIA's own Windows XP driver
for this chip. nv4_mini.sys carries the G86's complete PGRAPH context setup (context
microcode, golden context values, the register init list); its golden 3D state is the same
as nouveau's except three PGRAPH unit registers, and one of them is the triangle rasterizer
(TRAST 0x401c00: XP uses 0x042500df, every nouveau generation 0x044d00df for the G86) -
the natural suspect for pixels that huge triangles leave uncovered only at the largest
viewport. Two more registry-selected context variants, same mechanism as 3101 (no reboot):
  grctx4.reg = GrCtx 4: the proven 3099 context with only the three XP register values
               (TRAST, CCACHE 0x405000, 0x400844) - the minimal test, try it FIRST
  grctx3.reg = GrCtx 3: the XP way - XP's context microcode, XP's golden context, XP's
               register init list and unit init (clock gating, TPC 0x408000)
Install: copy nvmini.vxd to C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM and reboot once. Then: grctx4 + nvsky
(corner blocks? magenta?), grctx4 + nvhl at 1024x768 (holes?); then the same with grctx3
(a garbage screen or a hang is possible with 3 - it is the first run of NVIDIA's own
microcode under our manual context load; grctx0 restores 3099 without a reboot).
C:\nvtail.txt shows 'grctx variant N' and, for variant 3, 'grctx xp: 0x400800=...' (XP
only accepts chips answering 5049E8AC or 7EE17CC6 there - please send that line).

Build 3101 - 3100's context made the screen garbage on the T61 (nvsky 800x600 and
Half-Life; the first nvsky at 1024x768 after the reboot was clean). This build carries all
three PGRAPH context generations and picks one from the registry at every GL start, so
switching needs no reboot: HKLM\Software\vmdisp9x\vesa\GrCtx = 0 (nouveau 2.6.36, exactly
build 3099 - the DEFAULT, so installing 3101 restores the working driver), 1 (3099's
layout with only the three values current nouveau sets differently for the G86), 2 (the
current nouveau generation + zcull init = build 3100). Double-click grctx0.reg, grctx1.reg
or grctx2.reg, then run nvsky / nvhl; C:\nvtail.txt shows 'grctx variant N'. Install:
copy nvmini.vxd to C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM and reboot once. Please test in this order and say
what each looks like (a photo of garbage helps): grctx1 nvsky, grctx1 nvsky 800 600,
grctx1 nvhl; then the same with grctx2; grctx0 is the known 3099 behaviour.

Build 3100 - the 1024x768-only artifacts are small rectangular blocks of stale VRAM in
the screen corners: pixels that the huge, mostly off-screen triangles (sky faces, near
walls, floors) leave uncovered at the native viewport; Half-Life never clears its colour
buffer, so whatever was there shows through. The PGRAPH context the VxD loads at channel
start was generated from a 2010 nouveau; the current nouveau generator differs for the
G86 in a per-TP configuration value, the clipping-strand defaults and the 2D clip
defaults. This build loads the current context and also zeroes the zcull region
registers at init. nvmini.vxd changed: copy it to C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM and reboot. Tests,
from C:\NVMINI in a DOS box: 'nvsky' (wgltest 'sky' scene fullscreen 1024x768x16, cleared
to magenta every frame - any magenta block = uncovered pixels; then 'nvsky 800 600' to
compare), then Half-Life with plain 'nvhl' at 1024x768. In Half-Life, 'gl_clear 1' in the
console turns such blocks into the clear colour if they are uncovered pixels.

Build 3099 - 800x600 works now: the GDI pitch equals the hardware scanout pitch at
16/32 bpp (800x600: 1792 bytes, not 1600), which is what the GL present and DirectDraw
use for the screen surface - GL at 800x600 was a sheared, garbage picture before
(640x480 and 1024x768 have 256-byte-multiple pitches and were never affected).
nvmini.vxd changed (3098's complete submit drain + this): copy it to C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM
and reboot. The shim log now starts with 'vxd build / shim build', and nvhl appends
the VxD probe to C:\nvclk.txt, so a log says which VxD ran. About 'nvhl heaphi': it
is a 64 MB-heap diagnostic; Half-Life needs about 65 MB of textures, so with it the
sprites loaded last (HUD: health, flashlight) get no VRAM and draw wrong - that is
the heap, not a GPU bug. Use plain 'nvhl'; 800x600: nvhl -width 800 -height 600.

Build 3097 - the artifacts are WRONG TEXTURE PATCHES at 1024x768, absent at 640x480
(where the sampler rarely touches the big mip levels), unchanged by vsync/fullflush.
Two tests decide where the texture data goes wrong:
  wgltest driver mesa3d.dll window texcheck
      uploads 160 mipmapped textures (RGB and RGBA, ~45 MB like a level), reads
      every level back and compares, then draws 13 of them 1:1 and compares the
      framebuffer. Result box + wgltest_texcheck.txt (send it). Also try it at the
      game's size:  wgltest driver mesa3d.dll fullscreen width 1024 height 768 texcheck
  nvhl verify
      after every submit the shim reads back what the engines just read and
      compares it with the CPU copy: 'VRAM WARN' lines name the buffer.
  nvhl heaphi
      only the heap region above the GPU channel (3094 layout).
Also: the shim submits pending work and retries when an allocation fails (a level
load uploads thousands of textures between draws), 'nvhl vsync' accepts the raster
counter wrapping and logs its samples, and nvhl writes the clock registers to
C:\nvclk.txt. Send: C:\nvshim.log, C:\nvtail.txt, C:\nvkick.txt, C:\nvclk.txt,
wgltest_texcheck.txt.

Build 3096 - the occasional on-screen artifacts of 3095's Half-Life run: the driver's
self-checks saw nothing, so two switches let the T61 decide (both off by default):
  nvhl vsync      NVSHIM_VSYNC=1: the present waits for the panel's vertical blank before
                  the blit - no tearing, frame rate capped at the panel's 60 Hz. 3095 has
                  no vertical-blank sync at all, so fast turns tear.
  nvhl fullflush  NVSHIM_FULLFLUSH=1: whole-buffer flushes instead of 3095's range-directed
                  ones (slower). Artifacts that stay with it are not the flush ranges.
  nvhl vsync fullflush   both.
Please describe or photograph the artifacts: a horizontal seam during fast turns (tearing;
vsync removes it), a patch of wrong texture or lighting, or stray triangles.
New log lines: 'wgl: stats vsync waits/ms' and 'wgl: stats m2mf splits'.

Reading C:\nvshim.log (build 3094+): 'graph_units reg/used f3010001 f3010001'
= the GPU's unit mask was read (1 TP x 2 MPs); 'wgl: stats traps/warns' every
2 s must stay 0 0 - a 'KICK WARN' line means the engine was handed a buffer
that is dead or not yet written to VRAM (the 3093 untextured-cube bug), and
'kick TRAP' means the GPU faulted and the VxD recovered it.
Build 3095+: 'stats kicks mapwait/internal' = kicks the shim forced (expect ~0),
'stats submit ms' = time waiting on the GPU inside the VxD, 'stats kcyc
validate/kick' and 'kcyc flush/bo' = the shim's own CPU time in thousands of
TSC cycles; compare with 'present frames/ms' to see where a frame goes.

OPENGL (build 3046+)
--------------------
OpenGL programs get Mesa9x (llvmpipe, OpenGL 3.x/4.x software rendering)
through the ICD mechanism: opengl32.dll asks nvmini.drv for an ICD name
("SOFTWARE"), the registry maps it to mesa3d.dll. The INF writes the key; on
an existing install import d3dsetup.reg and make sure the mesa3d.dll in
C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM is the one from this package (3046+, built against this
driver's FBHDA API - the 2025 upstream one must not be used as an ICD).
Check: run wgltest.exe / icdtest.exe from the package (Mesa9x's test
programs); the renderer string should say llvmpipe / Mesa 25.1. Screen
savers "3D ..." and games using OpenGL should render.
